_rule: Prepared BEFORE the run (AGENTS.md), 2026-11-09, branch claude/hair-edge-still. Question: does rr_hair_strand_aa=2 lower the temporal flicker of strand edges after RR, once animation is excluded? One Test Dialogue1 launch (the only save the hair jobs use with strands large on screen; no idle out-of-dialogue save exists among the job generators), RTX Hair bundle on, rr_post=1, rr_hair_strand_snap_site=3, exposure held (qa_exposure_hold=1) for every burst. Eight 16-frame bursts with the RR inputs in ABBA ABBA order (off aa aa off off aa aa off: a linear drift of the dialogue cancels in mean(aa) - mean(off)), each after a 90-frame settle window in its own mode.
analysis: py -3 tools/hair_groom/edge_burst.py <8 burst dirs in plan order> --modes off,aa,aa,off,off,aa,aa,off; judged on final (what the user sees), rr_color reported

he1 audit (why this job).animation counted as flicker: edge_burst.py flicker = per-pixel temporal std / mean without motion exclusion; the band is the silhouette, so sub-pixel animation becomes variance there (the off bursts alone differed 30-80%). mc warps bilinearly and counts disocclusions at the same silhouette
he1 audit (why this job).no settle: he1 burst windows switched the mode and armed the burst 0.1 s after motion-ready: 0.31 s (burst-off-1, about 9 frames after a mode-2 window) to 2.3 s between the switch line and the arm (he1 04:02 log)
he1 audit (why this job).exposure free: he1 step() set qa_exposure_hold=0 in every window: bursts 15 s apart at different eye adaptation
he1 audit (why this job).mean of ratios: flicker averaged std / mean per pixel: dark background pixels of the band dominate

still pixels.definition: summed |rr_mvec| over burst frames 1-15 <= 0.25 px (edge_burst.STILL_PX: motion then adds <= 3% of a binary-coverage edge's variance)
still pixels.predicted: at least 256 still px in the band and the core of every burst at render resolution (the dialogue idles: head and hair sway, the body, background and parts of the hair edge hold still)
still pixels.invalid_if: a burst has < 256 still band or core px (edge_burst.MIN_STILL_PX): Dialogue1 cannot answer it, a still scene is needed

positive control (mode 2 applied in the.predicted: rr_color edge band hf of every aa burst below the off bursts' mean (he1 04:02: -13 to -15%)
positive control (mode 2 applied in the.invalid_if: an aa burst's rr_color band hf is not below the off mean: the resolve did not act in that burst (as in he1 d-aa)

settle.predicted: band_still drift (|first half - second half| / mean) of every burst within the off bursts' drift range: the RR history has converged after 90 frames
settle.invalid_if: the first burst after a switch drifts more than twice the largest drift of a burst that follows a same-mode burst

flicker (decision).metric: final band_still `still` = sqrt(mean temporal variance) / mean over the still band pixels
flicker (decision).predicted: aa/off -10% to -50% (offline accumulated edge flicker raw 0.0178 -> analytic 0.0086, -52%, with an ideal accumulator; RR rejects part of the history, so less)
flicker (decision).threshold: derived from the key-off repeats: sigma = sd(off) / mean(off) * sqrt(1/4 + 1/4); pass if delta < -2 sigma
flicker (decision).kept_if: PASS: band delta < -2 sigma, core_still delta within +-2 sigma (edge-specific), band_still mean within +-2 sigma (energy)
flicker (decision).rejected_if: FAIL with a VALID run: the band does not fall by 2 sigma, or the core falls with it, or the band mean moves by > 2 sigma

energy.predicted: band_still and frame_still mean aa/off within +-2 sigma of the off repeats (offline coverage-model bias +1.3% on the edge band)

cost.predicted: render-res chain about +0.18 ms in aa settle windows (he1 04:02)

disk: 8 bursts x ~0.55 GB = ~4.4 GB, a one-off pack: deleted after edge_burst.py has written its summary
